name: YARA compiled-rules memory scanning
description:
HARNESS RULES FOR THIS GROUP: (a) the MAIN PATH below runs on every input with the full input, exactly as listed; it is the baseline, the rest of this Logic Group only adds to it. (b) Entries marked 'same core / alternative' reach the same internal code as the main call: never replace the main call with them and never run all of them on every input (fan-out kills exec/s); if used, run at most one of them as an extra step chosen by spare input bits. (c) A configuration switch must never take inputs away from the main path; options that only add code (e.g. detail/verbose output) stay ON. (d) This list is incomplete; what the project's own fuzzers, tests and examples do with the target stays in scope. (e) Nothing the fuzz input can make slow or hang may run on every input: no allocation sized from an untrusted header field, no call with a known library hang (listed below), no callback/selector that aborts the main call for a large share of inputs; the bytes handed to the parser start at a fixed offset (offset 0 when the format has a magic number), so the fuzzer can find magic numbers and header fields.
MAIN PATH (keep on every input; verified in yara (qf-work/src/yara-c1) source):
1. LLVMFuzzerInitialize (once): freopen("/dev/null", "w", stdout) (yr_object_print_data prints with printf); yr_initialize(); yr_compiler_create; yr_compiler_add_string with ONE rule that does `import "dex"` and whose condition reads dex fields and calls the dex functions, e.g. dex.header.magic == dex.DEX_FILE_MAGIC_035, dex.header.checksum / data_size, dex.number_of_methods, dex.number_of_fields, dex.map_list.size, dex.has_method("<s>"), dex.has_method("<class>", "<s>"), dex.has_method(/re/), dex.has_method(/re/, /re/), dex.has_class("<s>"), dex.has_class(/re/) (libyara/modules/dex/dex.c:194-342 declarations, 337-342 the six function overloads), plus one short literal string; yr_compiler_get_rules; yr_compiler_destroy.
2. Per input: flags = SCAN_FLAGS_NO_TRYCATCH | (one control byte & (FAST_MODE | PROCESS_MEMORY | REPORT_RULES_MATCHING | REPORT_RULES_NOT_MATCHING)) (libyara/include/yara/scan.h:38-42). Take the control byte from the LAST input byte (or at most one fixed first byte) so the DEX header stays at a fixed offset of the scanned buffer, preferably offset 0. No variable-length prefixes.
3. yr_rules_scan_mem(rules, buffer, buffer_size, flags, callback, &state, 0) (libyara/rules.c:196-203), timeout 0.
4. The callback ALWAYS returns CALLBACK_CONTINUE. On CALLBACK_MSG_MODULE_IMPORTED call yr_object_print_data((YR_OBJECT*) message_data, 0, 1) (cli/yara.c:1231-1249; libyara/object.c:1073): it walks the whole object tree the dex parser filled. On CALLBACK_MSG_RULE_MATCHING walk yr_rule_strings_foreach / yr_string_matches_foreach.
Why: the dex module parses only when the scanned block is at least sizeof(dex_header_t) = 112 bytes and starts with one of the five 8-byte magics "dex\n035\0".."dex\n039\0" (dex.c:466-486, module load at dex.c:1529-1553). A callback that returns CALLBACK_ERROR for CALLBACK_MSG_IMPORT_MODULE destroys the module before it loads (libyara/modules.c:133-139). The previous LG harness returned CALLBACK_ABORT / CALLBACK_ERROR for 2/3 of inputs and never matched the magic once in 30 min (dex_parse_header, dex_parse, load_encoded_method/field never ran: dex.c 291 of 1001 lines).
Avoid `for` loops bounded by header size fields (dex.header.string_ids_size, method_ids_size, ...): they are untrusted 32-bit values and the loop runs that many iterations.
ADDITIONS on top (spare input bits only): a second rule with literal / nocase / hex / regex strings plus tags and meta (Aho-Corasick and match verification) and walking tags/metas in the callback; CALLBACK_ABORT only on a rare selector value and only for RULE_MATCHING messages, never CALLBACK_ERROR; a non-zero timeout only on a spare bit.

FEATURE DESCRIPTION (from the Logic Group stage):
yr_rules_scan_mem feeds an untrusted byte buffer to a compiled YR_RULES object: it creates a YR_SCANNER, wires in the caller's flags/callback/timeout, and runs the Aho-Corasick string-matching engine over the buffer followed by the compiled rule-condition bytecode interpreter. This is the core, security-relevant path of YARA: the buffer is walked byte-by-byte through the AC automaton (_yr_scanner_scan_mem_block), candidate hits are re-verified with regex/literal matchers (yr_scan_verify_match -> _yr_scan_verify_re_match / _yr_scan_verify_literal_match), and finally yr_execute_code runs the compiled condition bytecode which can trigger module parsers (yr_modules_load, e.g. pe/elf/dotnet/macho/dex modules) that further parse the same untrusted buffer as a structured file format. Bugs here (buffer overreads in AC matching, regex backtracking, bytecode VM, or module format parsers) are reachable purely from attacker-controlled scan input plus an attacker/engineer-controlled rule set and flags.
- yr_rules_scan_mem: target entry; drives the buffer through the scanner/AC engine/bytecode VM described above.
- yr_rules_scan_mem_blocks: variant entry taking a YR_MEMORY_BLOCK_ITERATOR instead of one flat buffer, exercising the same _yr_scanner_scan_mem_block core via multiple/partial blocks (and the ERROR_BLOCK_NOT_READY retry path).
- yr_rules_scan_file / yr_rules_scan_fd: variants that mmap a file/fd and internally call yr_rules_scan_mem, exercising the identical core with file-backed input.
- yr_scanner_scan_mem / yr_scanner_scan_mem_blocks: lower-level scanner API used directly by yr_rules_scan_mem*, useful to set extra scanner state (e.g. yr_scanner_set_flags/set_timeout/set_callback) before scanning the same buffer.
- yr_compiler_add_string + yr_compiler_get_rules: source functions that build the YR_RULES object (rules, including module imports like "import pe/elf/dotnet/math") from a rules-source string, so the fuzz input can also shape which AC strings/bytecode/modules are exercised.
- yr_rules_define_integer_variable / yr_rules_define_boolean_variable / yr_rules_define_float_variable / yr_rules_define_string_variable: configuration setters that populate external variables read by the compiled rule conditions during yr_execute_code, selecting different bytecode branches.
Input space: the raw scan buffer and its size (buffer_size up to and including 0), the `flags` bitmask (SCAN_FLAGS_FAST_MODE, SCAN_FLAGS_PROCESS_MEMORY, SCAN_FLAGS_NO_TRYCATCH, SCAN_FLAGS_REPORT_RULES_MATCHING, SCAN_FLAGS_REPORT_RULES_NOT_MATCHING) which toggle exception handling, entry-point computation mode and which CALLBACK_MSG_* reports are emitted, the `timeout` value which bounds the AC scan loop, the callback's return value (CALLBACK_CONTINUE/ABORT/ERROR) which changes control flow inside the scan loop, and the compiled rule set itself (string patterns - literal vs regex vs hex, module imports, condition bytecode) which determines which core code paths (AC transitions, regex verification, module parsers, VM opcodes) actually get exercised on the given buffer.
